actions.action: Commit deduplication and business updates together
actions.mechanism: A unique event key makes retries contend on one durable record; atomic commit prevents partially recorded processing.
actions.implementation: Insert the partner-scoped event ID and apply the update in one transaction. On conflict, skip processing. Acknowledge only after successful commit.
actions.check: Send concurrent copies of one event; verify one committed business update. Roll back processing and verify its deduplication insertion also disappears.
actions.risk: External effects require separate transactional coordination, such as an outbox.

actions.action: Guard entity updates with monotonic revisions
actions.mechanism: An atomic revision comparison prevents older or equal revisions from changing already newer entity state.
actions.implementation: For state-replacement events, update only when incoming revision exceeds stored revision, inside the deduplication transaction. Record stale events without applying effects.
actions.check: Deliver revisions 12, 10, 12 concurrently under different event IDs; verify final revision 12 and no stale or equal-revision effects.
actions.risk: Incremental events require ordered processing or gap recovery, not simply skipping revisions.

actions.action: Retain event keys through the seven-day boundary
actions.mechanism: A fixed first-receipt deadline covers the redelivery window without allowing duplicates to extend retention indefinitely.
actions.implementation: Store database-generated first-receipt time. Delete in batches only when database time strictly exceeds first receipt plus seven days; retain at equality.
actions.check: Replay just before and exactly at expiry: both must deduplicate. After expiry, verify cleanup and continued rejection of equal entity revisions.
actions.risk: Confirm seven days bounds arrival, not merely partner transmission; otherwise transit delay needs allowance.

actions.action: Budget actual deduplication storage below 2 GB
actions.mechanism: Compact records and measured database overhead constrain durable storage, rather than relying on raw event-ID size alone.
actions.implementation: Store only scoped ID and receipt time with essential indexes. Measure one million representative records; budget cleanup overlap and bloat. Stop admission before exceeding capacity.
actions.check: Load representative 64-byte-average IDs, exercise inserts and cleanup, and verify total allocated deduplication storage remains below 2 GB.
actions.risk: Never evict unexpired keys for space; reject without updating or acknowledging instead.

actions.action: Exercise crash and replay paths automatically
actions.mechanism: Fault injection verifies that acknowledgement loss cannot turn a committed event into a second business update.
actions.implementation: Kill processing before commit, after commit before acknowledgement, and during acknowledgement. Restart and replay each event, including stale revisions and boundary-time duplicates.
actions.check: Before-commit crashes must replay successfully; after-commit crashes must not repeat updates. Assert final state, effect counts, retained keys, and expiry behavior.
actions.risk: Mock-only tests can miss real database locking and connection-loss behavior.
